subject.title: fix(model-pricing): add DNS-resolution safety to pricing cache endpoint guard

question: Should optional model-pricing refreshes use an existing Gateway connection-time SSRF guard, or should the feature remain limited to its current static local-host policy until such a guard is available?
rationale: A standalone DNS preflight cannot establish the security property claimed by this PR; choosing the owner and semantics of the real outbound-connection boundary requires security and product intent.

options.title: Use a connection-time gateway guard
options.body: Route pricing refresh through a shared or newly explicit Gateway boundary that authorizes the address actually selected for the outbound connection.

options.title: Keep the existing static policy
options.body: Retain the current literal and local-DNS exclusions without claiming resolver-based rebinding protection until the Gateway has a suitable connection-time guard.

options.title: Permit the broader behavior intentionally
options.body: Accept the resolver mismatch and document that the pricing cache is not an SSRF-protected outbound-fetch surface.

recommendation.title: Use a connection-time gateway guard
recommendation.body: Route pricing refresh through a shared or newly explicit Gateway boundary that authorizes the address actually selected for the outbound connection.

likelyOwner.reason: The available review history routes the Gateway outbound-host security policy to this decision owner.
